fixed: CREATIONS no longer reads as a superscript (all three judges). It now stands on VANINDRA's baseline at 0.55 of the cap, under the same line, as the creative director suggested. This applies to lockup_horizontal_on_*, lockup_horizontal_header.svg, the global*.svg files and context.png. The recommended website header (wordmark_header.svg) leaves CREATIONS out, as the India and global judges asked. The stacked lockup carries CREATIONS centred under VANINDRA.
The step from heavy line to hairline used to fall over the last A's apex. It now sits in the middle of the A–C gap, never over a letter (global judge).

The S spur is gone. The S is redrawn as one continuous contrast-pen stroke (six joined cubics with smoothed weight), with no seams. It was checked at 4000 px, and the lower bowl is now optically larger (CD, global).

CREATIONS no longer reads as a stock grotesque. A, R and N now use VANINDRA's own leaf constructors (A's right arm, R's leg, the swelling N diagonal) at lower contrast. C and O have full sides with hairline tops and bottoms. The C is the O ring opened by a radial wedge, so its terminals are angled rather than flat-cut. The weight is retuned so CREATIONS matches VANINDRA's density (CD, India).

The mark no longer reads as 'a' with a macron (all three). The outer contour is now a V: a round shoulder under the line, a near-straight left arm and a sharp point at 95, with the danda running on to 100. The loop still never touches the line. At 16, 24 and 32 px the outline ends in a point (sizes.png). The V now shows in both the counter and the silhouette (construction.png).
Written rule: the व mark is the avatar for India and Hindi audiences only, and is never used alone in the USD workspace (CD, global).

New Latin-led avatar for South Indian and global accounts (India judge): mark_global_on_emerald.svg, mark_global_on_ivory.svg and mark_global_small.svg. The line runs full-bleed across the avatar and the system's leaf V hangs from it. A V under a short bar read as a nabla and was rejected.

Stacked lockup no longer shows two densities (CD, India). A new lockup cut of the mark (mark_lockup.svg) is used at 1.85×. Its strokes are within 20–30% of VANINDRA's, down from 2–3×: line 11.5 vs 8.8, danda 15.5 vs 13, loop hairline 6.3 vs 5. The two bars now match in weight instead of competing.

Phone header at a 17 px cap (CD, global): new pixel-fitted cut, wordmark_phone_17px.svg (111×19). Every letter origin, stem and the line sit on whole pixels: N stems 2 px, I/D/R stems 3 px, hairlines 1.7 px. The N diagonal is heavier than its stems, so the word no longer reads VA-IIII-DRA. Checked at 7× in header.png.

Hairlines ghosting at real size (global): a new sturdy cut (wordmark_header.svg) has hairlines of 10.2 units, stems 16 and N stems 12. It is used for the 28 px desktop header, the context.png header bars and the Reel credit. No stroke in these is under 1.5 px.

Embroidery (global): the sturdy cut's hairline is 1.63% of the word width (1.14 mm at 70 mm). Size rule: embroider VANINDRA at 62 mm wide or more. Never embroider the master wordmark. Embroider the full name only at 180 mm or more.

Global version: the caps used to stand clear of the gold hairline (global judge). They now overlap it by 55% of its thickness, so the caps visibly hang from it. The old pale anti-alias seam is gone (checked at 5×).

Reel tag (CD, India): the line now starts at the E of EDIT BY, at the safe margin (30 px on 540, 60 px on 1080), not at the frame edge. EDIT BY stands on the hairline, which steps up to the heavy bar that VANINDRA hangs from. EDIT BY is drawn in the system (credit cut: stems 2.2 px, hairlines 1.6 px), set in ivory. VANINDRA uses the sturdy cut. The credit sits inside the 3:4 grid crop.
वनिंद्रा, न (India): the left tick is now a short teardrop of about 0.26 H, down from 0.36 H, in line with Martel and Noto. It no longer drifts toward त.
वनिंद्रा, ि and ं (CD, global): the ि hook now lands on न's danda, and the anusvara sits above that danda (over न) instead of past it.

वनिंद्रा, द्र (CD): द is redrawn as one pen stroke. It leaves the line as a danda-weight stub, turns left into a hairline top arm (the entry hook), runs down a heavy left side and around the bottom, and ends in a terminal at the lower right. The rakaar is a caret hung from that terminal: a leaf leg down-left and a hairline leg down-right. The व in the word uses the new mark geometry. It was compared side by side with Martel and Noto Serif.

All deliverables were re-rendered in the _final_final folder after at least three render, look, critique and revise loops (loops2/ has the loop renders, explore_final.png the studies). Updated: every BRIEF §6 file, plus reel_tag.png, header.png, global.svg/png, sizes_global.png, context_global.png, construction.png and rationale.md with a full size-rules table and risks.
not_fixed: Native-reader sign-off on वनिंद्रा (all three judges): I cannot do this myself. The fixes are drawn and checked against Martel, Noto Serif and Tiro, but the file and rationale.md still say the Devanagari must be verified by the team or a native type reader before any public use, and the bilingual files stay optional until then.

Global judge's alternative of widening the V counter until it dominates: partly rejected. I made the silhouette a V instead and kept the counter at its size, because widening it further thins the loop below 2 px at 16 px. Ruling the mark out of the USD workspace (also offered) is done.

Global judge's option to hang CREATIONS on its own line under the hairline: rejected in favour of the baseline placement the CD and India judge proposed. A second rule under the name reads as an underline and adds a second line, which was tested in Round 3.

The CD's 'do not hang it from a hairline step' is met by moving CREATIONS to the baseline. The step itself remains as the line's two-weight grammar, but it now falls in the A–C gap, and nothing hangs from the hairline step in a lockup.
story: In Devanagari every letter hangs from one line, the shirorekha ("head-line"), and at VanIndra everything we make hangs from its headline too: the first three seconds.
construction:
Everything is parametric (r4system.py holds every number; built with skia-pathops; all text outlined; every SVG under 14 KB). Units: VANINDRA cap = 100, from the top of the line to the baseline.
- Mark (r4mark.va_vloop): line 9.5, danda 13 at x=58. The loop leaves the danda at y=20 as a 5.5 hairline. Outer shoulder at (2,40), then a near-straight arm to a sharp point at (31,95); counter shoulder at (17,43). Return stroke 10.5 meets the danda at y=54; the danda runs on to 100. The V shows in both the counter and the silhouette.
- Other mark cuts: small (line 13.5, danda 17, 55% ink) and a lockup cut (line 6.2, danda 8.4, used at 1.85× over the name).
- Wordmark: master unchanged (line 8.8, stems 13, hairlines 5, leaf diagonals). Sturdy cut: hairlines 10.2 (1.63% of width), stems 16, N stems 12. Phone cut: the sturdy cut snapped to a 17 px pixel grid.
- CREATIONS: built from the same constructors (leaf A/R/N, contrast-pen C/S, superellipse O). Set at 0.55 of the cap on VANINDRA's baseline under the same line, which steps to a hairline at mid-gap.
- Global: one gold hairline over both words, with the caps overlapping it by 55% of its thickness.
- Global avatar: a full-bleed line with the system's leaf V hanging from it.
- वनिंद्रा: drawn with the same pen and leaf rules.
- Reel credit: the line starts at the safe margin, EDIT BY (drawn credit cut) stands on the hairline, and the line steps up to the heavy bar VANINDRA hangs from.
Generators: build2.py, header2.py, reel_tag2.py, construction2.py.
concept_name: Shirorekha, final: Everything hangs from one line (final-final polish)
weaknesses: The Devanagari (वनिंद्रा, especially the द्र proportions, the ि hook length and the anusvara position) was still drawn by a non-native designer and needs native sign-off before public use.
The new pointed bowl is even closer to Bengali ব (ba/va, the same historical letter). Harmless, but some Bengali readers will read it that way.
At 16 px the व mark is still 'a drawn glyph' to Latin readers. That is why a separate Latin avatar and a usage rule are needed, which adds system complexity.
The global avatar is an initial V. It is ownable only because of the full-bleed line; if someone shortens or boxes the line it becomes a generic nabla or monogram.
Six cuts (mark: master, small, lockup; name: master, sturdy, phone) need usage discipline. The wrong cut at the wrong size brings back ghost hairlines or a mark that is too heavy.
The full-name lockup deliberately leaves a gap between the hairline and CREATIONS. Someone may 'fix' it back into a superscript.
The C/S of CREATIONS and the द are sampled pen outlines: smooth at display sizes but node-heavy. A vector-editor cleanup and a hand-hinted ICO are still recommended.

fixed: Header and Reel misreads ('Van'ndra', 'Varlndra', 'Varnndra'), raised by all three judges: the hinge was rebuilt as a staircase. 'Van' sits on line 1 and 'Indra' on line 2, and the n's right leg drops straight down into the I. Both letters stay whole, so nothing is hidden and nothing reads as an apostrophe. The header uses this staircase in its small cut: 64 px tall on desktop (31 px cap) and 44 px tall on phone (21 px cap). I checked both at 3-4x pixel zoom (header.png). The Reel credit uses it too (reel_tag.png, reel_tag_light.png). The one-line rising-I hinge is retired: once the I came down to the ascender it read 'Van'ndra' even at display size (explore.png, studies 1-2).

Avatar read as 'nl', 'rl' or a mirrored h, all three judges: the profile picture is now the staircase in a circle (mark_on_emerald.svg). It reads 'Van Indra' at 320, 150, 110 and 56 px (context.png, sizes_mark.png). At 48 px and below, the favicon is the wordmark's own V in a heavier cut (mark_small.svg, mark_small_tile.svg in the browser tab). It is clean at 16, 24 and 32 px (sizes.png).

Shoulder cut 16/46 units closed in one colour below about 18 px, with dark lumps at 16-32 px (all three judges): fixed by removing the cut. No part of the system depends on a hairline cut any more, so every one-colour version holds.

The I's top at 784 against V 700 and d 724, with the widest slab (CD): the I is now exactly ascender-tall. Line spacing = ascender 724 - slab 21 = 703. Its slab extension went from 37 to 31 so it matches the feet. The meeting point is drawn as one slab with two serifs: brackets up for the n's foot and down for the I's head.

Ball terminal a, beak r, the t's top jutting like a flag, s ending in blunt slabs, mixed terminal styles (CD, India, global): every free stroke end is now the same straight knife cut rising about 20°, on a, r, s, C, e, t and y. The t has no flag and the s ends are lighter. The Devanagari ends the same way.

Stacked lockup read as two equal words; tight 'ns' (India): Creations is now at 58% of the name's cap height in its own heavier optical cut, right-aligned under Indra. The 'ns' kern went from -4 to +14.

No Indian root and no Devanagari (all three judges): वनिंद्रा is drawn in the same pen, with heavy dandas and falling strokes, a light shirorekha and rising strokes, and knife-cut ends. It is not Tiro pasted in; Tiro was used only to check where each stroke attaches (loops/ref/tiro_grid.png). It appears in wordmark_devanagari.svg and lockup_bilingual_on_ivory/emerald.svg, marked 'to be verified by the team'. Public story line: Hindi writes the same n+i join as one sign, नि, so the gold I in English is the gold ि in Hindi. The spelling is वनिंद्रा in every file. A grep found no बनिंद्रा in any concept file.
'Edit by' was set in a stock grotesk (CD, global): 'edit by' is now drawn in the system, with new b and y glyphs added (reel_tag_*.svg).

Antique-gold I disappeared on light footage (global): on light footage the credit is now all emerald (reel_tag_light.png). Ivory with a soft-gold I is kept for dark footage (reel_tag.png). Both sit at left 30 px / top 150 px, which is inside the 3:4 profile-grid crop and clear of the caption overlay.
On emerald the gold was only a 3 px tick (India): in the staircase the whole visible I, including its shared slab, is gold. It is never a sliver.

Embroidery rule wrong by more than 2x (global): I recalculated it with a real 1 mm test (render at 10 px/mm, morphological open with a 1 mm disk). The staircase in its small cut passes at 90 mm wide or more; at 60 mm the V hairline and the arch tops vanish. Caps and narrow placements use the V at 12 mm tall or more. Creations lockups are never embroidered below 250 mm. These rules are in rationale.md.

New size rules, file map and risk list are in rationale.md. Every deliverable was re-rendered from the drawn sources: vitype.py, deva.py, build.py, extras.py, construction.py, explore.py and render_all.sh.
not_fixed: 'Carry the gold down the whole I stem, or go one-colour below 40 px' (India): I did not do either literally because the problem behind it is gone. In the staircase the whole I is visible and gold, and the one-line hinge that produced the 3 px gold tick is retired.

Genre: still a high-contrast editorial serif (CD, India, global). This is only partly addressed, on purpose. The knife-cut terminals, the staircase and the drawn Devanagari move it out of the ball-terminal DTC-beauty look. I kept the contrast and the bracketed serifs because all three judges praised that craft under 'what works'. Rebuilding the letters in a different genre would have thrown away the parts that were rated well.

The one-line hinge was not kept as a display-only feature. Its two fixes contradict each other: at 784 the I looks pasted in (CD), and at 724 it reads as an apostrophe even at display size (explore.png 2b). The idea now lives in the staircase, and the one-line wordmark sets n and I side by side, with the gold I marking the join.
The avatar at Instagram's 32-40 px comment and story sizes is a texture, not readable text. Instagram serves one image at every size, so the V cannot be swapped in there. This is noted as a risk.
story: VanIndra is one name made of two words, and the logo shows the join: the n that ends Van runs straight down into the I that begins Indra, so one stroke belongs to both. For Hindi audiences (to be verified by the team): Hindi writes the same join as one sign, नि, so the gold I in English is the gold ि in वनिंद्रा.
construction: Every Latin and Devanagari glyph is drawn from béziers, straight segments and pen-expanded spines (vitype.py, deva.py). No font outlines appear in any deliverable. The staircase puts 'Van' on line 1 and 'Indra' on line 2. The n's right leg continues down into the I, and the slab where they meet is bracketed both ways: the n's foot and the I's head in one piece. Line spacing = ascender 724 - slab 21, so the I is exactly ascender-tall. Gold is only ever the I (and the ि in Devanagari). Every free stroke end is the same knife cut, rising about 20°. There are two optical cuts: display (hairline 24, stem 82) and small (hairline 34, stem 90), plus a heavier favicon V. Creations is drawn in the same system at 58% in a heavier cut. वनिंद्रा follows the Latin pen: heavy dandas and falling strokes, a light shirorekha and rising strokes, knife-cut ends. The ि hook is the n's arch facing forward. Deliverables: mark.svg, mark_on_ivory.svg and mark_on_emerald.svg (staircase avatar), mark_one_colour_gold.svg, mark_one_colour_emerald.svg, mark_small.svg, mark_small_ivory.svg and mark_small_tile.svg (V favicon), staircase.svg, header_staircase_*.svg, wordmark.svg, wordmark_mono.svg and wordmark_small.svg (one line, ligature released), wordmark_devanagari.svg, lockup_horizontal_on_ivory/emerald.svg (Van / Indra Creations), lockup_stacked_on_ivory/emerald.svg (Van / Indra / Creations), lockup_bilingual_on_ivory/emerald.svg, reel_tag_ivory.svg and reel_tag_emerald.svg, global.svg and global.png. Renders: sheet.png, sizes.png, sizes_mark.png, context.png, header.png, reel_tag.png, reel_tag_light.png, construction.png and explore.png. All are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-vanindra-creations/704148cb-74ad-5713-93e9-04b0ce97a9f0/scratchpad/logo2/r3_hinge_final/ and are rebuilt by render_all.sh.
concept_name: The Hinge: VanIndra, one stroke for two words (staircase)
weaknesses: A two-line signature is unusual. One-line placements fall back to a wordmark with no ligature, only the gold I, so the idea is weaker there. The staircase is about 2.2:1, wider than a typical stacked block.
At Instagram's 32-40 px comment and story sizes the staircase avatar is a texture; it reads from 56 px up.
The favicon is a plain V, the most default move available. It is defensible only because it is limited to 48 px and below.
The Devanagari was drawn in code by a non-native hand. द्र's drop and crossing strokes, the ि hook height, the bindu position and the knife-cut danda feet all need native verification before use.
It is still an editorial high-contrast serif. Its ownability rests on the staircase and the gold I rather than on the letterforms.
Embroidery needs at least 90 mm of width, so small merchandise has to use the V.
It has not yet been tested with real readers; a 5-second 'what does this say?' test is recommended before the vote.
